title: T-107 Slice 1 — MECH_02 ¡ESQUIVA! on the v2 contract (adapt EsquivaMicrogame)
description: Slice 1 of the TASK-034 (GDD T-107) split. Adapt the v1 EsquivaMicrogame.cs (the 4-player one-hit-eliminates FFA dodge sim — NOT DodgeSim/Esquiva-3D, which GDD §10.4 keeps as a View/style reference only) to the canonical §10.2 v2 IMicrogame contract: engine-free Core sim, injected SeededRandom, zero-alloc steady Tick, normalized [0,1]² arena. HAZARD PATTERNS (human-ruled 2026-07-07, engineering [ASSUMED] geometry, reviewer-verified, human tunes at UAT): Rain = hazards fall top→bottom; Sides = enter from left & right edges; Cross = diagonal corner→opposite corner; Homing_soft = drift toward nearest player with turn rate capped 30°/s (escapable by construction). Min spawn separation 0.08; one hit eliminates; ranking by survival tick with GDD shared-elimination + timeout-survivors-share-1st rules. Declare difficultyScaling params in the v2 definition; pass the TASK-030 validator. Conserve or migrate existing dodge tests.
acceptance_criteria: MECH_02 implements the canonical v2 IMicrogame contract as an engine-free Core sim with injected SeededRandom and zero-alloc steady Tick; normalized [0,1]² arena.

The four hazard patterns are implemented per the ruled [ASSUMED] geometry (Rain top-down / Sides L-R / Cross diagonal / Homing_soft slow-turn toward nearest player, 30°/s cap), each [ASSUMED]-tagged; no overlapping spawns (min separation 0.08).
Escapability test: an optimal bot survives the full duration on every seed in the test set (Homing_soft's 30°/s cap guarantees escape).
Result is Ranked by survival tick; simultaneous eliminations share Place and survivors at timeout share 1st, with no fabricated winners.
The v2 definition declares difficultyScaling params and passes the TASK-030 validator.

Tests-first (red captured before impl); existing dodge tests conserved or migrated; fast suite green, no regression; legacy consumers keep compiling. StagePresenter/View wiring is out of scope (separate §10.4 work).

comments.author: dev-t101
comments.body:
Hand-off. Two commits: ddd2978 test(core) -> dc81602 feat(core). Baseline 561 -> 576/576 (15 new).

PROCESS HONESTY FLAG: did NOT follow strict clean-slate tests-first. Designing the escapability bot required the RenderState shape to exist, so a first-draft impl was built before the suite's first run. That first run WAS genuinely red (3/14 failing on real defects); every subsequent fix was mutation-verified (break it, confirm the specific test fails with exact quoted output, revert). Flagging plainly rather than dressing up as a clean red-first cycle. Commit order is test-then-impl (ddd2978 before dc81602).

ESCAPABILITY BOT (AC1/AC3 headline) — 6 genuine iterations, each a real bug in bot or sim: (1) inverse-distance repulsion + octant-snap limit-cycled on Cross seed 16; (2) discrete wall/hazard priority modes -> boundary itself oscillated on Sides seed 2 -> Schmitt-trigger hysteresis (enter wall-mode at 0.2, exit past 0.35); (3) wall-mode ignoring hazards walked into one on Rain seed 13 -> immediate-danger override; (4) repulsion-sum buried the escape signal under equal-opposite Cross diagonals -> REPLACED with one-ply lookahead (evaluate 8 Direction8 + None, maximize resulting min-distance to any hazard); (5) lookahead myopic on HomingSoft seed 4 -> reintroduced wall-hysteresis as a STRATEGIC layer over the tactical lookahead; (6) HomingSoft seed 9 failed for a production reason, not a bot flaw.

REAL PRODUCTION BUG + [ASSUMED] FIX (needs review + flagged for human ratification): HomingSoft hazards never naturally exit the arena (they chase in-bounds players, unlike Rain/Sides/Cross straight-liners), so over 8s they accumulate unbounded — seed 9 had 5 simultaneous perfect pursuers = inescapable pile-up. GDD's escapability guarantee is about ONE hazard's 30°/s cap, not an ever-growing swarm. FIX: HomingSoft hazards get a 4-second lifetime cap ([ASSUMED], NOT GDD-literal, documented as such). Load-bearing production design decision, not test tuning.

TURN-CAP ISOLATION: the main sweep uses avatarSpeed 0.35 > hazardSpeed 0.15, which ALSO guarantees escape by raw speed regardless of the cap (verified: removing the cap still passed). Added a SECOND adversarial test hazardSpeed 0.25 > avatarSpeed 0.2 to isolate the cap's own necessity — mutation-confirmed it genuinely fails without the cap (seed 0, "Expected: False, But was: True").

AC1: v2 IMicrogame contract, engine-free, zero-alloc steady Tick (value tuples are structs, no new in hot path; GetResult per-round alloc matches the established v2 class). AC2: 4 patterns per ruled geometry, each [ASSUMED]-tagged in enum + class doc; min-separation 0.08 via bounded retry deferring spawn to next tick (verified it mattered: Cross's 4-corner geometry could otherwise force a violation — checked via slot-identity tracking, not RenderState's repacked list, after a naive all-pairs check gave a false positive). AC3: escapability green — general sweep (4 patterns x 20 seeds) + turn-cap-isolation. AC4: Ranked by ticks-survived desc, shared-place-on-tie; both GDD edge cases (simultaneous elim share place; timeout survivors share Place 1) fall out of the one rule with zero special-casing, dedicated tests + a mixed-ticks no-fabricated-winner test. AC5: MechanicParamSchemas.Mech02Esquiva added (spawnRatePerSec/hazardSpeed ranges, reserved hazardPattern/jumpEnabled) per Mech04Apunta pattern; 2 tests (valid passes, out-of-range hazardSpeed fails). AC6: v1 EsquivaMicrogame + its tests UNTOUCHED (zero diff); v2 test file comments which v1 scenario each carries forward.

SCOPE DECISION: jumpEnabled declared in EsquivaParams/schema for completeness but the jump/dash mechanic is NOT implemented — GDD names it a per-definition variant, escapability is guaranteed by movement (turn cap) alone, no AC names jump behavior. Documented in the class doc as an explicit scope decision. Stayed off v1 Esquiva, DodgeSim/Esquiva-3D (View-only), and StagePresenter/View wiring.
